column4: [ASUS][B3B5P5][PTL] Under UEFI, WiFi disconnection during downloading recovery image
column49:
1 driver issue fixed and 1 BIOS TCP level configuration change:

1. driver fix:
IWL_TX_DMA_MASK was set to 0xFFFFFFFFF (36-bit), a leftover from gen1
code. GEN2 and future devices support full 64-bit DMA addressing and
TFD addresses.

The PciIo->Map() function can legitimately return addresses above
36-bit, but TransTxqBuildTfd() rejected these valid addresses,
silently dropping TFD entries while advancing the TXQ write pointer.
This leads to firmware assertions and TXQ watchdog timeouts.
The fix removes the obsolete 36‑bit DMA mask and the associated validation check, allowing proper handling of 64‑bit DMA addresses.

2. See WIFI-645065 regarding HTTP buffer size

column4: [HP][IEC][Merino][Win11 25H2][PTL][WhP2/GfP2][SIO2455614] Device sometimes cannot connect to WPA3-Enterprise EAP-TLS Unifi AP
column49:
AP behavior:
After STA G3, the AP retains the old session state and has an SA Query in progress. As a result, it correctly rejects the STA Association Request with status 30 (comeback). The STA waits for the comeback interval and then retries the association. At this point, since the interval has elapsed, the AP should accept the request. Instead, the AP sends a Deauthentication frame with reason code 6 (CLASS2_FRAME_FROM_NONAUTH_STA), which is non-compliant behavior.

Why the reconnect fails:
The driver correctly treats reason code 6 as recoverable and initiates a fresh connection attempt. However, a race condition in the driver can cause this retry to fail, leading to “No suitable network found” / “No enabled networks,” and don't try to do actual connection.
In addition, when we retrigger a connection, we are not preserving the connect token, so even if we'll be able to connect the driver will eventually fail. Fix both issues.

column49: In the scenario where SAR is changing, GMPD will request paging. But when TAS is enabled, GMPD doesn't care about SAR limit since TAS can decide to ignore SAR limit, so GMPD must calibrate without SAR consideration. So when SAR has changed, GMPD requested paging. But if TAS is enabled, GMPD won't build a new plan. The bug is that if a plan is not built, GMPD won't relinquish the paging request - creating a never ending paging request (low LTR). column4: [HP/MachuN][IEC][LNL/Fmp2/24H2] Intel BT PCI Enumerator show YB after Force Shutdown (long press power key 10 sec) with enable AMT (PP2/LP3) in AC mode
column49:
WiAMT loads its WiFi FW very early (before BIOS runs),
WiFi FW runs FSEQ. As part of FSEQ it sets FINE locks (in particular AUX_HW_LOCK_2)
There is a logic in the top that prevent HW to write to registers when AUX_HW_LOCK_2 is set and relevant func_state is LOW
Relevant logic preventing BT OTP Reader (usee BT UMAC master) writing to Aux while BT func_state is LOW:
bt_umac_aux_connect_we_func_lock    = (~scu_aux_hw_lock_2 || bt_scu_func_state) && bt_umac_aux_connect_we;
When BIOS switches BT I/F to IOSF, BT HW kicks BT OTP Reader
OTP Reader tries writing to Aux register to enable OTP, but fails due to the early lock (BT func_state is LOW on this HW stage)
All next reads from OTP are failed since OTP is not enabled
BT config space remains with default values. In specific Sub_System_ID = 0x0000
OS doesn't load BT driver due to Sub_System_ID missmatch

solution: TOP-14807: Don't set AUX_HW_LOCK_2.

column49:
Bug root cause:
 - There are 2 active macs - BSS client and P2P client.
 - UMAC send 2 protection windows to LMAC - one for each mac.
 - LMAC start the first protection window.
 - Beacon is received, and LMAC remove the first protection window.
 - LMAC send NTF to UMAC that beacon is received.
 - LMAC allow PS.
 - PHY move to PS mode.
 - UMAC update 1 of the protection windows timing, and send it to LMAC.
   Since the current beacon event wasn't not removed yet, the UMAC send
   its window as well.
 - LMAC received hiscorical protection window, and set protection.
 - To configure the chain ant req, LMAC need to access the PHY.
   Since the PHY is in PS mode, we get assert when trying to access the PHY.

Fix:
If phy is not exist, coex status is off.
Check if coex status is not off before starting coex protection.

RC is the same as bug WIFI-527459. Fixed on: https://gerritwcs.ir.intel.com/c/wcd_fw-dev/+/177112

column4: [Panasonic] C-state does not enter C10 when DC powered, screen on and AP not connected
column49: The bug was caused by a new module (called internally 'DSM'), which is responsible for a system that organizes data efficiently. We noticed that when another part of our system, the scan module, asked the DSM for permission to use that data, the DSM attempted to complete the request but was interrupted by entering a low-power mode. This interruption prevented the process from finishing properly, lowering the LTR and allowing the machine to enter its own low-power state. We've updated the system so that the DSM can continue to manage these requests even if it goes into low-power mode, which should resolve the problem.

column4: [Dell][Compal][Arches][MTL][AX211][BSOD-0x13A][Netwtw14!memFree] WB with BSOD prvDptfAgentGetTemperatureCb
column49:
During execution, the mCtdpGetCurrentTemperatureApi stores provided callback arguments in CTDP context. Since this API relies on the FW response to get the current temperature from FW, this response may take time (as in this case - JS is busy). So when the next caller calls this API, it replaces the previously stored callback's arguments with its own. And that's what happened here. 
When the response started executing and working with the context, the memory that CTDP context is pointing to was already released by the next caller because of failure in sending FW command (transport layer was closed already). And this caused to the BSOD.

column49:
[BUGFIX]  Coex: Fix Sync2Bt Timer Loss Sync

(-) Bug:
     Sync2Bt Timer is keep expired since in the past and prevent any LMAC other activity.

(-) Bug Description:
    Sync2BT Timer is use sync2BtRise-Timestamp in order to set the next timer expiration..
    But when the Sync2BtRise-Timestamp is in the past and not advanced for a long time
    it result with continues Sync2BtTimer expired and actually prevent any LMAC other activity

(-) Bug Scenario:
     Sync2Bt is enabled & working on timer, WiFi is on LB
     During that, WiFi is triggered Calbrations on HB which result with Phy LB Deactivate
     and Aux Phy Activate on HB. Following that on FullCoexOff we set Sync2BT Disable reason = SYNC_2_BT_BT_PROTOCOL_DIS
     Status: Sync2Bt is enabled from BT Side but since we are on HB now the Disable reason should allow all Tx but the tracking should continue.

    Then following mailbox we get to sync2BtEngineStatusUpdate() with sync2BT enabled status.
    but on _sync2BtEngineUpdatePtaInterrupts() since we ask for sync2BtEngineIsSync2BtAllowed() we disable the sync2Bt kick filter
    while the Sync2Bt machnisem (timer) is stiil working.

Bug Solution :
  (-) Remove the dependency of sync2BtEngineIsSync2BtAllowed on _sync2BtEngineUpdatePtaInterrupts.
       Following that  as long as Sync2BT is enabled the Sync2BT mechanism will keep working even when we enter to HB Phy.
       Only in case Sync2BT is disabled (by BT MBX or by CI change) the Sync2BT mechanism will disabled.
       Note - When Sync2BT mechanism is working but Phy is on Non LB (Aux\Calib) the Tx will allowed and not defered.

  (-) Disable Sync2Bt Timer & Enable Resync by Sync2Bt by ISR.

column49:
by Chigirincev, Dmitry:

When we receive data, the rate of ack/BA calculation is based on rate from RX packet
on of the parameters in the rate is antenna selection

the calculation of antenna selection in ack is based on RSSI of RX packet

In CCK there is a bug, that we first make decision of what antenna to use and only after that read rssi of rx packet from registers

In this case the RSSI in the decision is 0 for both antennas and in this case (when rssi is equal for both antennas) our algorithm takes antenna B always (not shared antenna with BT).

So the solution is to read rssi values of rx in right place, and only then make decision what antenna to use

column4: [HUAWEI][HUAQIN][MorganG][Intel RPL][Intel AX 211][WIFI][Win11]The call to the IntelIHVPipeClient interface failed, causing the computer cloning function to fail.
column49:
Since PC migration doesn't call FreeLibrary for MurocApi DLL, the destructor that suppose to close PIE and PipeClient threads is not called. It's an incorrect behavior by the PC migration.
Up until 22.220, PIE and PipeClient used CreateThread API to open those threads, threads that are created using this API are closed (not gracefully) when the process is closed.
In 22.230, CreateThread API was replaced with std::async API, threads that are created by std::async must be closed before closing the process, otherwise the process will keep running.
In order to mitigate such an incorrect behavior, we changed std::async back to CreateThread.

column4: [Intel][RPL-P][AX211][BE200][UEFI_3.2.25] With WPA2 authentication, UEFI throughput drop 80% than Open/WPA3
column49:
firmware expects that driver will pass management frames on Tid=15 and UEFI driver wrongly use Tid=7.
When AP sends ADDBA Req, UEFI driver builds the ADDBA resp and pass it to firmware (Tid=7) then firmware does not handle it properly (there are different handling specifically for management frames on Tid=15) and when the connection is WPA2+11w disabled, the protected bit and CCMP header is set by the firmware on the ADDBA response (frame is sent unencrypted).
Some AP's may ignore it and we'll not experience low TpT, but other AP's may not ignore it and the block ack session will not be valid and this will lead to low TpT.
Fix it by use correctly Tid=15 for management frames.

column4: [HP][Win11][CFL][ThP2][Tobago][BSOD 0x124] System hang up with black screen and BSOD 0x124 occurred when running S3/S4 stress test
column49:
cc51: ca0d5c43533964b034e84aa44a9e9c037269729e
Not needed for any other core (yet), seen on ThP only.

Flush PCI pipe before completing the PNP_SET_POWER task.
Fix for a race that was found on weak CPU/PCI, where
driver is writing into a CSR, however, the actual right occurs
after we complete the PNP_SET_POWER task.
This causes WHEA unrecoverable error and leading to BSOD 0x124.
Due to weak CPU, or might be a combination with multiple
PCI bridges on this platform, the actual write is not instant.

For some reason, issue was not seen on Win10, while stated appearing
on Win11 - might be different PCI error handling logic.

Deeper analysis: it was seen using PCI analyzer that after driver
is completing the PNP_SET_POWER task, OS puts the PCI in low power mode,
and no further transactions are allowed. However, then we see a memory
write TLP - our CSR write, which was obviously initiated before.

As a WA, need to “flush” the PCI, by reading from the last written CSR
before competing the task. This should ensure that all previous
transactions have completed and it is safe to put PCI into sleep.

column4: [HUAQIN][ASUS][AX211][RPL][22H2][22.200] System cannot connect to specific AP (But RTK, QC WLAN PASS)
column49:
The bug occurs with known misbehaving AP which advertises ECSA with CS-to-self
in its probe responses (not in beacons)
We saw this behavior in the past and implemented  DCR-261 (WREQ-36392) which allows us to connect to such APs
But in this setup the AP advertises operating class = 0x1a (26) while we’re in China MCC domain 0x434E (I see this in the RLG log didn’t find Country IE in AP beacons/probes)
According to the table E-6 in Annex E in the spec this operating class is invalid for China
So when we try to determine if the ECSA contains CS to self we attempt to retrieve the band by operating class + channel number, and since such operating class doesn’t exist
 in the current MCC we conclude that the CS is not CS to self, since the band is different (INVALID_BAND) though the channel number is the same
and thus we exclude such candidate and don’t connect though our competitors such as QCOM and RTEK do
The system requirement was to ignore the operating class in this specific case and assume the same band as the old one

column49:
[BUGFIX] mvm: don't account for the losing time of the wrong link

    When we want to look for a hole for an event, and our event is placed
    after event B, we want to make sure that we leave room for the link that
    runs event B to loose the medium properly before we run our event.
    In case of GO / BSS in SCM, we can have the following scenario:

    GO's beacon saver ends at 100
    BSS'es TBTT ends at 50

    This means that we could place an event at 101 since the losing time of
    the GO is 0, but we don't since we want to leave enough time for the
    losing for the client.

    This wouldn't be a big problem if we didn't have to re-allocate events.
    I saw in USIM the following problem:

    1) time is now 50
    2) GO / BSS in SCM, beacon of the GO is at 150, beacon of the BSS at 100
    3) Fragmented scan allocates events (50 ms long)
    4) We place one time NOA for a fragment of the scan at time 180, after
       the next beacon of the GO (because of the beacon saver)
       Note that this overrides the BSS's TBTT which is fine.
    5) the beacon saver event of the GO ends at 180 to give room for the
       scan event
    6) time passes by, we are at 100
    7) TBTT of the BSS runs and we remove the occurrence after beacon Rx
    8) Refresh
    9) we place again the the scan's fragment, but this time we place it at
       180 + BSS's losing time.
    <=== This is the bug ===>

    We just moved the fragmented scan's event, but we had a NOA that was
    placed exactly for that specific event and now the fragmented scan's
    event is unfortunate because of the beacon saver of the GO.

    We could have placed the fragmented scan's event again at 180 because
    the client already knows it needs to have left the channel by 180. But
    because we take into account the losing time of the BSS after an event
    that belongs to the GO, we delay the scan event by 4ms and it misses the
    window created by the GO's NOA.

    Fix this by looking at the losing time of the link of the specific event
    that precedes the hole, and do not consider all the events in the
    binding.

column4: [Huawei][Quanta][H99E][NobelF][AX201][21H2][WLAN] [AX201][805737181 ]After the WiFi driver is upgraded to version 160, there are more than 900 unknown threads in the message center, which are always blocked, and this problem occurs only after the driver i
column49:
Those threads are opened by a "KeepAlive" timer which runs a function every second to check if the connection to RPC is still valid.
The connection to RPC check is done by running an API that is sent to the RPC server, if the API fails, it returns an error.
When the Wlanext.exe process is in "pending" state, the RPC server doesn't respond to the RPC call which blocks the call forever (Bug in MSRPC).
Since the call is blocked, and the timer is still running, every second another thread is being stuck, and this is why there are so many threads.
To solve this, I put a boolean that signals if there is already a running thread, if there is already a running thread, the function will exit without doing anything.

column4: [HUAWEI][HUAQIN][MorganF][Intel ADL][Intel AX 211][WIFI][Win11]The PIE service has stuck cause to GetSupportedChannels does not return a value.
column49:
PIE is using an asynchronous method in order to send a bind event, in this case there was a racing condition between that method and the FreeLibrary call:
1) Asynchronous method is called.
2) Router frees the PIE IHV module while the method is still working.
3) The asynchronous method is still working while the main thread of the DLL that host that method is closed.
4) This causes Wlanext.exe process to remain open.
5) On driver enable, a new Wlanext.exe process is created.
6) Since there are 2 running Wlanext.exe processes, this means that the RPC server is still working in the old process which prevents creating a new RPC server connection in the new process.
7) PIE service tries to connect to the RPC server which is stuck on the old process, which makes the service to also be stuck.

column49:
The WiAMT requested the NIC ownership and this triggers the
LOST_OWNERSHIP Serializer flow. As a part of the flow MAC_ADD_MODIFY FW command
for BSS MAC deactivation is issued.
For some reason the command caused a FW assert and the
Serializer receives request to run the RESET flow.
But the Seriazlier ignores the reset request by design being in the middle of
the LOST_OWNERSHIP flow.
Thus the serializer is stuck waiting for the Deactivate BSS completion callback
which is not called since the command ACK from the FW didn't arrive due to
the assert. And it doesn't recover form this state
The solution is to flush the TX Cmd queues upon reset request in case we're in
the LOST_OWNERSHIP flow, which would call the command callbacks and complete the
RF Kill for all the modules

column4: CLONE - [HUAWEI][HUAQIN][KelvinC][Intel CML][Intel 9560][19H1]Test SUT will frequently disconnect from the network when connect to the H3C router.
column49:
Debug has shown the INA controllers become stuck in illegal state, in which there can be no preamble detections until the RX is reset. This happens when packets are received in high input power and the receiver is reset while such packet is still on air.

We traced the cause to a combination of INA HW bug and a long-existing FW workaround:

There’s a config register called CCK_PURE_11B which disables the OFDM preamble detector. It was originally intended to be used with APs that support CCK only without OFDM. Since it was considered an esoteric feature it was not thoroughly validated.
Due to HW bug, if CCK_PURE_11B=1 and there’s high incoming power which leads to AGC Fast Step, it’s possible for the preamble detection module to remain turned off when it’s supposed to turn on. Whether that happens depends on relative phase between 2 clock signals when entering a specific state of the controller FSM. Having the preamble detector turned off instead of on prevents detection, and it also prevent restoring the gain to max since the controller waits for the detector to indicate that preamble wasn’t found. It’s only possible to exist this state by toggling rx_en, or if CCK detection is not required as in HB.

column49:
Debug has shown the INA controllers become stuck in illegal state, in which there can be no preamble detections until the RX is reset. This happens when packets are received in high input power and the receiver is reset while such packet is still on air.

We traced the cause to a combination of INA HW bug and a long-existing FW workaround:

There’s a config register called CCK_PURE_11B which disables the OFDM preamble detector. It was originally intended to be used with APs that support CCK only without OFDM. Since it was considered an esoteric feature it was not thoroughly validated.
Due to HW bug, if CCK_PURE_11B=1 and there’s high incoming power which leads to AGC Fast Step, it’s possible for the preamble detection module to remain turned off when it’s supposed to turn on. Whether that happens depends on relative phase between 2 clock signals when entering a specific state of the controller FSM. Having the preamble detector turned off instead of on prevents detection, and it also prevent restoring the gain to max since the controller waits for the detector to indicate that preamble wasn’t found. It’s only possible to exist this state by toggling rx_en, or if CCK detection is not required as in HB.

column49:
[BUGFIX] Sending delete key cmd to FW

Description: In master, the FW (Data Path) controls the key table, but in core43 (Thunder,
our case) the Driver controls it, except for D3 then the FW (WoWlan and DP) controls it.
Before the security refactoring driver sent add_sta_key command with delete key flag for every key on disconnection flow.
During the refactoring, FW requested not to send add_sta_key command with delete flag on disconnection and FW will clean the sta key when removing the station (there is a special handle for this request on driver code). Driver will only clean internally.
FW don't delete the key in its table (BUG!)  when the driver do delete it in his parallel table keys,
leading to scenario in which after more than 15 rekeys in D0 and eventually rekey in D3, FW can't find empty key index although there are free indexes.
According to Lotem Bar-yaakov, the issue is not trivial to solve on FW side, we deliver a fix on driver:
1. send delete FW command in case of release peer
2. send delete FW command with the Old key index in case of adding new key in re-key flow.

The issue wasn't seen before because we don't have a test with the scenario above.

+ FW - see in attached gerrits

column4: [Dell][Compal][Olympic][CML U][BITS454023][BSOD-0x7E][Netwtw08!prvTidQueueRemoveReadyHead+0x4b]Stress_WB_BSOD
column49:
[BUGFIX] Fix rare race between remove peer and tx scheduler assign

Description: There is a rare race but still possible due to module design and implementation.
1. Core 0: Got a packet for peer/tid (0,0). This is the only packet for the queue
2. Core 0: Packet pass classification and processing. Packet on ready state AND scheduler was not triggered yet
3. Core 1: Remove peer flow triggered
4. Core 1: Flush flow doesn't send command to FW (no scheduled packets) and return the packet sync.
5. Core 1: Remove peer flow release peer schedulers (nothing to do as no scheduler was assign)
6. Core 1: Remove peer completed
7. Core 0: Continue the flow calling txResourcesMgrAssignTxScheduler regardless if there are (or not) packets and if peer still exists.

Trying to allocated a scheduler for a non-exist peer will cause unexpected behavior -> assert or BSOD.

The fix:
Check if peer still exist without calling txResourcesMgrAssignTxScheduler

This a rare race with multiple preconditions in order to reproduce.

This issue only occurs on HE connection due to HTC support bit in HE MAC capabilities.
Galaxy S10 decides to turn on the 'Order Flag' bit in the DHCP frame control flags due to this bit.
This bit means that the MAC header has 4 additional bytes of HT Control (HTC).
The LLC comes right after the MAC header in the packet.
The OS complains that the LLC is invalid, even tho in pass/fail cases the LLC is the same.
If we remove the additional 4 bytes of HTC the connection succeeds.

column49:
A channel switch which entered the sequential queue before an invalid change op
mode task on an undefined port, caused the driver to return success status on
the change  op mode task, thus continuing a flow while the context is null.

	1. BSS completes TASK_CONNECT.
	2. GO needs to channel switch, this task is entered to sequential queue.
	3. OS sends TASK_CHANGE_OP_MODE on port 0x3 (which is invalid), this also enters the sequential queue.
	4. We complete the TASK_CHANGE_OP_MODE while on the channel switch task context, thus return success to OS.
BSOD occurs since we now get tasks and have no context which handles them, since
 from driver side TASK_CHANGE_OP_MODE never succeeded.

Fix it by passing the return status to the CB of create VIF

column4: [ASUS][AMD][X712DA/X712DK][8265] Wake on WLAN by magic packet sometimes fails
column49:
Wowlan feature is based on preventing WLAN MAC Reset during S3 and S4 – keeping the mac alive while the Host in S3/S4 therefore the mac can receive the magic packets and wake the host.
The WLAN reset prevented by using a control signal called “Persistence”. 
Persistence == (Device in D3 ) & (PME_EN) == Power Management  Control / Status Register (PCIe CFG space) bits [1:0] (PowerState)  & bits [8]  (PME_ENABLE)
The bug in WLAN device is  that : Power Management  Control / Status Register (PCIe CFG space) bits [1:0] (PowerState)  was reset during entry to L2 , due to race condition which cause the internal LTSSSM machine to move into Detect State 
Instead of staying in L2 State.
Once the LTSSM moved to Detect the  power state changed to D0 and Persistence was cleared. 

The WA provided is : before going to D3 the WLAN FW receive an indication for the Driver that host is going to D3. In addition to other process the FW “force the persistence “ to ignore the D3 conditionץ
This keeps the MAC from getting the RESET .

The Bug was fix in later silicones after WsP/8265 (fixed over ThP/9260 and newer products).

column4: [HP/SIO1758846/CFL/W10/CCP2/Superman] WiFi shows "No Internet" about 4 mins then available in network UI after restart unit with wifi connected
column49:
AP send Addba request and imeddiatelly after that M1 EAPOL (SN0) 
Driver receive addba request and starting to open aggregation with FW and send Addba response 
When driver receive first EAPOL (M1) the open aggregation flow doesn't finished, and driver handle M1 as normal packet (not AGG) 
driver send to AP M2 EAPOL, and AP send to driver M3 (SN1) 
when driver receive M3, the Open aggregation flow already finished, and driver store M3 (SN1) in reorder buffer (SN0 is missing in reorder buffer, because was handled as normal packet) 
second after that AP send new M3 (SN2), driver see that packet SN1 is aged, and notify to OS 2 M3 packets 
OS answer to first of them with M4, but AP expect to M4 for second M2 


The Fix: Upon connection establishment (encryption ready), answer ADDBA response with decline status, and only after connect aggree to aggregation

Root cause:

AP send Addba request and imeddiatelly after that M1 EAPOL (SN0)
Driver receive addba request and starting to open aggregation with FW and send Addba response
When driver receive first EAPOL (M1) the open aggregation flow doesn't finished, and driver handle M1 as normal packet (not AGG) 
driver send to AP M2 EAPOL, and AP send to driver M3 (SN1)
when driver receive M3, the Open aggregation flow already finished, and driver store M3 (SN1) in reorder buffer (SN0 is missing in reorder buffer, because was handled as normal packet)
second after that AP send new M3 (SN2), driver see that packet SN1 is aged, and notify to OS 2 M3 packets
OS answer to first of them with M4, but AP expect to M4 for second M2


The Fix: Upon connection establishment (encryption ready), answer ADDBA response with decline status, and only after connect aggree to aggregation

column4: [Dell_Compal_Centenario_ICL_DVT2][AX201] WLAN won't re-enable after unplug lan cable from dock
column49:
we didn't indicate to OS that SW radio state have been changed to off.
the scenario was as follows:
1. radio is on
2. driver received HW RF kill (radio changed to off)
3. driver received SW RF kill (radio is still off)
when we receive RF kill that changes the radio state, we send indication to OS that contains the radio state status of SW and HW.
on 2. we sent indication.
on 3. we didn't send indication because there was no change in radio state.
OS waited to get our indication and kept sending us SW RF kill oids.
the fix was to send indication every time we get an SW/HW RF kill.

column4: [Asus][CFL][W730] 9560 BT  throughput too low with 20.110 UWD BT driver (0.5Mbps)
column49:
Due to historic HW issue on BT (BT only catch the interrupt rising edge so need to toggle it after writing data to MBX in order BT will get interrupt to our MBX.), there is WA for handling this issue that is done by using shrMbx infra : 

o Read Status register of WIFI2BT. ---------->[ int1RegVal = (shrMbxHalIntrRead(MAILBOX_ID_WF2BT) ] 
o Clear Status register of WIFI2BT. ----------> [ shrMbxHalIntrClearBits(MAILBOX_ID_WF2BT, MBX_REG_DEFAULT_BITMASK) ] 
o Write to Cause register what we read & the new type we send now (DBGC MSG) --> [ shrMbxHalIntrWrite(MAILBOX_ID_WF2BT, (g_typesToSend | int1RegVal) << 8) ]. 

This write will set interrupt status bit and triggers interrupt rising edge for BT. 

This above handling is done by using shrMbx Infra which is wrong due the READ & CLEAR function always approach BT2WIFI registers (offset from CNVI_AUX_MBX_MASTER_0_TO_1_STATUS) instead of WF2BT. 

In bug WIFI-16623 this issue caused us to miss mbox rcv messages on power up flow since on power up flow we send DBGC message before handling the rcv messages and because of the bug we clear the interrupt bit of BT2WF instead of WF2BT. 

In this scenario we got mbox message of TYPE2 and we try to send mbox message of type7. Before sending it we read the interrupt status register of BT2WF (instead of WF2BT) and we get bit2 set since we got mbox TYPE2 from BT. Then when we write to WF2BT status register we add the value we read (bit2) so BT gets interrupt of message TYPE2 although we didn't intend to send such message, and it reads data reg7 which contains garbage and ATS bit it set there.

column4: [Lenovo-IdeaPad][Inhouse][KBL-R][Yoga930][RS5]WiFi icon shows limited connection after resume from MS, but it can auto recover in 30~60secs
column49:
When D3 flow starts, driver does not close RX
aggregations. D0 (FW) code doesn't close them as well, but D3
code sends DELBA frame to AP (on all opened TIDs). This actually
tells AP that we close all recipient aggregations, but DRV and D0 code
remain in the 'old' state, where aggregations are still open.
The problem starts when we move back to D0. For DRV after resuming
from D3 AP will try another ADDBA on an existing TID, when FW D0
code runs still with open aggregation window and AP sends single frames

column49:
Description: Due to wrong calculation of TFD->count, we can enter into an infinite loops while dispatching.
In case of fake TX response for single packets, prvTfdQueueInvalidateTail is called and it will (finally, after many TXs) decrement TFD->count below zero (or to a large UINT32).
When reset comes, DP aborts all committed packets (txTidQueueAbortCommitedPackets) and will fetch queue->count (numOfPendingEntrys).
Trying to dispatch this huge number will result in commutative DPC WD BSOD (0x133_1).

The fix:
1. to guard TFD->count. add additional checkers (prvTfdQueueInvalidateTail)
2. single TX complete (prvTfdQueueSendComplete) check also command response sequence number (TFD index) and make sure it is equal to TFD->tail driver has

column49:
Our FW can access shared block in the CRF side either in direct call or indirect call method.
The direct method access directly the CRF address.
The indirect method access an indirect HW in the CNVi which trigger the actual access to the CRF. Its purpose is to prevent CPU stall due to long access of direct access to the CRF.
It is forbidden to have both methods mixed, as otherwise unexpected behavior can happen.
Our WiFi FW code has transitioned all the access to indirect method, however we have found that one API was missed and still used a direct method.
The fix is to transition all APIs to the indirect method

WDI RX flush CB is sent via job.
A mutual deadlock was found in RX flush flow when miniport reset and WDI RX flush are running in parallel cores. In this flow, one core is in the middle of miniport reset and waits for all DPCs to end rvIsrWaitForAllActiveDpcsToEnd). The other core is running DPC DPC (ECHO_RSP RX) calling RxFlushConfirm. This indication goes to WDI which stalls (CompletePendingCancelSendsOrHaltJobs) and waits for the reset to complete causing a mutual deadlock for two cores waiting one for each other.

column4: [Huawei][Mach][WLAN] BSOD occurred when PC is doing S3/S4 stress testing
column49:
When loading FW the, driver triggers WD on FW load.
In case FW load WD expired, the NIC SM enters ERROR state, before resetting FW it waits for all DPCs to complete (inside the NIC SM lock)
In case the FW load complete DPC is handled on a different core, it will try to take the NIC SM lock in order to indicate the NIC load complete event, this causes a deadlock between the thread that has the SM lock waiting for the DPC to complete and the DPC thread that is waiting for the SM lock.

Fix was to split the NIC SM reset event to 2 steps. Step one waits for all DPCs to complete inside a job (async)
This will avoid the wait for DPC to wait while taking the NIC SM lock.
Once wait for DPC is over, NIC ever RESET_STEP_2 will be triggered to continue FW reset

column4: [Huawei][Mach][WLAN] BSOD occurred when PC enables Wifi hotspot
column49:
Drain runs in a job and after calling internal TX CBs.
When complete is called prior to calling internal TX CBs, peer can be removed by GO, before drain complete is called.
This can happen when GO sent DEAUTH frame to peer and drain started (in case of shared Q).
TX complete will come and will call drain complete, which will remove peer from DP DB and destroy the GO client's SM.
Later on, this frame will be forwarded to GO which will try to dispatch it into the SM which was destroyed earlier.

The fix:
1. Always call drain complete after calling internal TX CBs
2. Make sure that drain complete starts new JOB in order to break the stack
and make sure that jib runs last

column4: [Huawei][Kepler][WLAN] BSOD DPC_WATCHDOG_VIOLATION (133) during stress test
column49:
When loading FW the, driver triggers WD on FW load. 
In case FW load WD expired, the NIC SM enters ERROR state, before resetting FW it waits for all DPCs to complete (inside the NIC SM lock) 
In case the FW load complete DPC is handled on a different core, it will try to take the NIC SM lock in order to indicate the NIC load complete event, this causes a deadlock between the thread that has the SM lock waiting for the DPC to complete and the DPC thread that is waiting for the SM lock. 

Fix was to split the NIC SM reset event to 2 steps. Step one waits for all DPCs to complete inside a job (async) 
This will avoid the wait for DPC to wait while taking the NIC SM lock. 
Once wait for DPC is over, NIC ever RESET_STEP_2 will be triggered to continue FW reset

column49:
TFD Q tail invalidation protection.
Due to wrong calculation of TFD->count, we can enter into an infinite loops while dispatching.
In case of fake TX response for single packets, prvTfdQueueInvalidateTail is called and it will (finally, after many TXs) decrement TFD->count below zero (or to a large UINT32).
When reset comes, DP aborts all committed packets (txTidQueueAbortCommitedPackets) and will fetch queue->count (numOfPendingEntrys).
Trying to dispatch this huge number will result in commutative DPC WD BSOD (0x133_1).

The fix:
1. to guard TFD->count. add additional checkers (prvTfdQueueInvalidateTail)
2. single TX complete (prvTfdQueueSendComplete) check also command response sequence number (TFD index) and make sure it is equal to TFD->tail driver has

Reconfigure LQ after resuming from D3
When resume from D3 is complete, there is a need to reconfigure (reset) LQ. Currently LQ "reconfigure" flow is distributed among all the VIFs, bound to several events and doesn't have a single flow.
The correct place is probably to do it from DP MAC reconfigure, however, this change cannot be currently done in the scope of a bug fix.
After resuming from (connected) D3 there is no LQ reconfigure and it is assumed that TLC will converge based on TX responses.
Statistics collector ignores all TX responses, since belonging to older 'color' (rateTableID) preventing from TLC to upscale and open AGG.
The result is basic rates in TX, no AGGs and long pings.

The fix is to unset the lowest rates which were set during D3 entering flow without resetting station's LQ.
The reason not to reset is since no LQ command can be sent anyway so need to wait to TLC convergence based on TX responses.

column4: [Dell/Compal][CNVi][CFL/9560/RS2] Very Poor JfP2 performance
column49:
WDI: max supported SGLs (per NBL), use 19 instead of 8
Current capability to WDI is to support up to 8 SGLs per NBL.
This value is hardcoded, since 'normal' NBLs should not have more than this value.
However, in case of LSO, we can exceed it, since we support up to 32 KB LSO size, where each SGL is limited to page size (4 KB). 
In such case, where NBL has more than 8 SGLs, WDI will drop it. (it will try to 'fix' it, and might fail).

The fix for CC30 is to enlarge this value to 19 (MAX_TBs - 1). The maximal NBL which we can transmit (in case we do not copy it) can contain 19 SGLs.
This is a HW limitation (ThP and below) for the TX command. TBs array has 20 entries.

The fix for main will have different logic: driver will not limit this value and will be support up to 0xFFFF (infinity).
In case we are getting NBL with more than MAX_TBs - 1 SGLs, driver will drop it (or copy). In such way, the drop will be monitored and visible.

column4: [Xiaomi][ARL][HrP2/AX201][i5-11320H] LE Ext Adv scan result delay more than 20s+ sometime, very low performance compare with MTK chipset with BT24.10PV
column49:
Root cause:

We are switching to secondary channel only when primary offset is lesser than secondary offset. This is wrong, this will result in two problems,

When we received the primary packet at the beginning of the scan window, and it has a valid far aux offset. we will end up switching to secondary channel though secondary offset is still far. This makes bad utilization of remaining scan window and end up with fewer primary packet detection.
 When we received the primary packet at the end of the scan window, and it has a valid far aux offset. we will end up switching to primary channel though secondary offset is near. This makes secondary job to get into past and eventually we release the entry from scan data base. This will add delay for the detection for the secondary PDU.

column49:
The issue was in the function that handles the TX for the packet
header.
A race condition between the BMC pushing data towards BRI MP FIFO,
while the CSR write to TX modem TX FIFO (over BRI LP FIFO) did not
arrive to the CRF.
This causes, under specific timing conditions, cause the TX FIFO reset
to arrive to the CRF after the first MP BRI data (18 bit) arrive to
TX FIFO, leading to corrupt data seen over the other end.
This fix adds BRI dummy read before pushing bits through the BMC.
to ensure BRI CSR FIFO drains completely before triggering the
transfer, preventing the race condition.

column49:
WiAMT loads its WiFi FW very early (before BIOS runs),
WiFi FW runs FSEQ. As part of FSEQ it sets FINE locks (in particular AUX_HW_LOCK_2)
There is a logic in the top that prevent HW to write to registers when AUX_HW_LOCK_2 is set and relevant func_state is LOW
Relevant logic preventing BT OTP Reader (usee BT UMAC master) writing to Aux while BT func_state is LOW:
bt_umac_aux_connect_we_func_lock    = (~scu_aux_hw_lock_2 || bt_scu_func_state) && bt_umac_aux_connect_we;
When BIOS switches BT I/F to IOSF, BT HW kicks BT OTP Reader
OTP Reader tries writing to Aux register to enable OTP, but fails due to the early lock (BT func_state is LOW on this HW stage)
All next reads from OTP are failed since OTP is not enabled
BT config space remains with default values. In specific Sub_System_ID = 0x0000
OS doesn't load BT driver due to Sub_System_ID missmatch

Solution: AUX_HW_LOCK_2 (bit [8]) in SCU fine locks register (cnvi_scu_cnvi_scu_lock @0x6EAC).

column4: [Xiaomi][RPL/ARL][AX211][i5-11320H] LE Ext Adv scan result delay more than 20s+ sometime, very low performance compare with MTK chipset.
column49:
Root cause:

We are switching to secondary channel only when primary offset is lesser than secondary offset. This is wrong, this will result in two problems,

When we received the primary packet at the beginning of the scan window, and it has a valid far aux offset. we will end up switching to secondary channel though secondary offset is still far. This makes bad utilization of remaining scan window and end up with fewer primary packet detection.
 When we received the primary packet at the end of the scan window, and it has a valid far aux offset. we will end up switching to primary channel though secondary offset is near. This makes secondary job to get into past and eventually we release the entry from scan data base. This will add delay for the detection for the secondary PDU.

It is observed that host driver is timing out as it is not getting ACK
for D0 entry doorbell interrupt in some corner case scenario during
stress test. It is confirmed from the debugging that controller was
getting doorbell interrupt but not getting sleep control status bit

previous state and if this is detected as transition, then sleep
control doorbell bit in the status register is set and processed as
if this bit is set by hardware.

column4: CLONE - [Lenovo ThinkPad JP][Thames2/LnL/FmP][QS][PCIe] BT Device lost due to TOP exception during S4 cycle - Clean WA from FW/Driver to retrieve debug

While executing a D3 scenario, prior to entering D0, we observed incorrect PCIE context info, which we suspect is due to an unidentified bug in the hardware. Consequently, the firmware (FW) triggered a fatal exception, leading to a soft reset of the CPU. During this soft reset, we encountered an additional Top exception rewriting all original exception data that was alraedy recorded in persistent.

The details of this Top exception suggest an issue that occurred during the initialization of the FSEQ following the soft reset due to original exception. However, the extra details provided by the Top exception data was inconclusive as per Top team. We assume that the hardware may have already been in a bad state due to the original issue when FW attempted to program the FSEQ as part of the initialization after the soft reset.

Due to the current exception handling approach, we lacked adequate data for debugging.

Proposed Solution: To address this issue, systems suggested halting the CPU immediately after any exception occurs. This will allow the host to collect debug information related to the exception before the firmware proceeds further and trigger further exceptions due to any instability already in the system.

column4: [Samsung][Odin2-15/TGL/HrP2] Multi-Control (SPP) cannot connect to android tablet. (cherry pick fix of DUT sends LMP_Set_AFH as a peripheral)
column49:
Peer is accepting connection and making role switch.
Role switch is passing good however, Intel DUT (Peripheral now) is
sending LMP_Set_AFH following the role switch.

The root cause for this issue is a race between the processing of
RS message and lmp-accepted-for-host-conn-request-packet.

RS and LMP don't pass the same flow:
Role switch related messages:	BC-> LC-> LLC-> LM
PDU packet reception:		BC-> LC-> LM

Since PDU packet reception has fewer steps than RS, LM may move to the
new role (slave role) too late.
When lmp-accepted-for-host-conn-request-packet is received at LM,
LM layer can still be in the old role (master)
i.e., LM is in old role, and LC is in the new role.

As a fix, the setup complete process is postponed till RS message is
processed by LM layer.

column4: [HUAWEI][HUAQIN][Morgan][Intel TGL][Intel AX 201][BT][Win11]The DUT connect fail with phone during running stress test(FW Fatal exception and Hardware error observed)
column49:
During pairing process, while calculating the DHkey, locally generated
key handle for that particular BR/EDR link to be fetched and validated.
To fetch the keyhandle( pertaining to the link), we pass link index, and this
index was wrong, resulting in fetching a wrong key handle for that link.

Wrong index is fetched, because the Array(au8SSPDHKeyRequestedId) holding
the identifiers has duplicate entries. But this array is expected to have unique identifiers
for each and every BR/EDR link.

Why Array has duplicate entries, because array is updated with identifiers
by incrementing a static variable( u8NextSSPDHKeyCalcId),in multiples of 2.
And this variable is unsigned integer which can hold a maximum of value 255.
And in case of multiple pair-unpair operations, this variable will wrap around.
So we may end up with duplicate entries in the array.

column13: v22.50.0.2 PV PHBTW28375 for Samsung SmartThings
column49:
Windows BT stack does not use LL Privacy yet. Hence, it is responsible for periodic refreshing of the random address of ADV instances it owns. The period is assumed to be 15 mins with a margin of +-1min. The address refresh works fine when the PC is in S0. But, when the PC is in Modern Connected Standby, Windows BT stack stops refreshing the random address due to a bug. This causes Privacy issue (device is trackable as the MAC address remains same for as long as the device is in Modern Standby) as well as a breakdown in SmartThings functionality.
Controller resets the GATT Instance Addr field in Offload ADV instance Service Data if the address has not been refreshed for an hour. The address in this field is used by the remote device to identify the connectable ADV coming from the same device. Even though a connectible ADV is present, due to the field being set to 0, the remote device cannot connect to the device causing SmartThings functionality to breakdown.
Privacy issue in Windows platforms can only be fixed by MSFT. So, that is out of scope of this jira ticket. The fix here is to make sure that SmartThings functionality will still work with the accepted loss of privacy.
The fix done is to not reset the GATT instance MAC address field on PID rotation 1 hr timer expiry while GATT ADV instance is still enabled for advertising.

column49:
Problem statement: As part of system preparation using sysprep.exe and generalization in Windows Audit mode, the Bluetooth driver resulted in YB.

Background: The Intel Tile Node is a raw PDO that exposes interface for Tile application to send request to Driver though IO CTL interface. The raw PDO will appear as hidden device in Device manager under Other devices section without any device properties. OEMs raised a concern about the new node also requested to populate device properties for this node to adopt in the OEM Automation / testing. As part of adding the Device Properties for Tile Node, the Intel Tile Node device is made as child device for Bluetooth driver node to inherit all the properties of Parent. To achieve this, ibtusb.inf is modified to represent Tile Node as Null Device and child of Intel Bluetooth Driver.

Analysis: As part of Driver installation using MSI, the package will install all the drivers that are included in it . This is a PNP installation requirement to support Plug and Play of devices. The MSI will install all the driver including CcP and HrP which contains the Tile Node INF entries though the platform having TyP connected. The Driver will included the firmware for respective SKUs only. After Installation in audit mode and then performing Generalization, It is observed that Windows OS is loading different SKU driver Binary ( in this case it is CCP) where the TyP firmware will not be present. Due to this, the driver will result in Yellow Bang. This has been confirmed form the driver logs.

This has been narrowed down further by uninstalling the CcP and HrP SKU drivers manually after installation and then performing the Generalization in audit mode. In this case, the Windows OS is loading the driver Binary for the respective SKUs.
Few more points:
- Bluetooth Driver name (ibtusb.sys) and INF(ibtusb.inf) is same for all SKUs .
- The Intel Tile Node INF Entries are present only in HrP and CcP. These drivers are installed as part of MSI package and which binds the Tile node with ibtusb.sys/ibtusb.inf ( Additional clarification required here from MSFT )
- The issue is narrowed down only. However, the root cause of the issue still need to be investigated based on feedback from MSFT. We have Open sighting with MSFT PnP team on this (https://hsdes.intel.com/appstore/article/#/16012307683 ).

Test Coverage: As part of Test coverage, all the testing including the installation is performed in Normal windows mode. Switching between Normal OS to Audit mode and then Generalization is not covered. This is the process followed in Factories for imaging the platforms. This is the gap identified and is required to add testing coverage in Install domain areas.

column4: [Asus][Huaqin][UX425UA][AMD_LCN][CCP][FW Exception] Intel Bluetooth show yellow bang when run S4 stress test
column49: The function mbx_ReadMessages() is using delay function MBX_SEMAPHORE_RETRY_DELAY_uSEC(4); before getting semaphore. The delay function MBX_SEMAPHORE_RETRY_DELAY_uSEC(4); is implemented based on the slot and bit counter value. These registers are not accessible when active park is enabled. When active park is enabled, these registers always give zero value and the delay loop will enter into infinite loop and it will trigger watchdog timeout exception. To fix this issue, replaced the delay function MBX_SEMAPHORE_RETRY_DELAY_uSEC(4); with simple "for" loop delay which eliminates dependency on special registers for the purpose of introducing delay.

column49:
When there is a quick transition from USB suspend to resume from host, wakeup interrupt may be already set while processing suspend. In addition on CNVi designs, at the end of suspend processing during partial power down entry, suspend_n signal is asserted, This signal goes as input signal to U2U bridge. In such corner case condition, wakeup may be triggered before programming PPD setting or after programming the PPD setting. If
wakeup is detected before programming PPD setting, FW don't allow PPD entry. If PPD entry setting is done by the FW,  this fix ensures the worst case propagation delay required for synchronizer logic (4 * 32KHz clock cycles period) before PPD exit setting is programmed. This ensures suspend_n de-assertion is properly propagated (through synchronizer logic) to U2U bridge and UTMI clock switches are stabilized.

column4: [Samsung] The status of BT devices is changed as paired and connected repeatly
column49:
FW is designed to start guard timer when LC while programs BC job. This guard timer is to detect if job could not begin, and initiate recovery procedure and re-invoke pre-processor.
In case of this issue, job was started correctly, and LC_WAKEUP_MSG was posted by BC layer, and lc_preProcessor was stared, but before stopping guard timer, AFH channel classification/aging algorithm is invoked which is taking 700+ uS.
In the meantime, guard timer expired and as part of recovery mechanism, it cancels current and next job, which is incorrect.
On the other hand, BC layer (unaware of guard timer expiry) continues with current ongoing job. This sometimes results FATAL exceptions or connection timeouts depending on BC state when guard timer ISR was invoked.

Fix:
On receiving LC_WAKEUP_MSG, lc_preProcessor should first stop guard timer and then run the AFH channel/classification/aging algorithm
BT-20550 is created to identify root cause

In a LE-Link, as Master the Link State is updated to LC_LE_LINKSTATE_PHY_UPDATE_PENDING even before transmitting the PHY_UPDATE_IND PDU (i.e. when the PDU is queued).
If the PHY_UPDATE_IND PDU transmission gets delayed because of other items in the transmission queue or because of NACK, then there is a chance that the linkstate will be updated back to ACTIVE (as part of lc_LECollectRequest), since the PHY Update Instant is not filled in the PDU untill the PDU is picked for transmission.
And when the PDU is actually picked for transmission, the linkstate is no more PHY_UPDATE_PENDING, it is ACTIVE and this results in Instant not filled in the PDU, which can cause the remote device to terminate connection upon reception of this PDU and result in Connection Loss.

WHQL failures reported in this Issue are due to FW watchdog exceptions. One of the LE Scan transaction has corrupted endTransaction native slot programmed, which caused all subsequent jobs to be incorrectly programmed. When this happens, LC scheduler will not be able program BC layer and start a job, and just keep running LC Preprocessor forever until WD exception occurs.

LE scans are of 37ms window size. If controller gets a sync within this window, then LC scheduler will try to program another LE Scan window for the time remaining in the 37ms window.
It looks like the issue (incorrect end native slot) happens while programming the second LE scan window. when very little scan window is left for the second scan transaction

Fix:
As we know that the endTransaction native slot is getting corrupted, a check is added if the duration of the Current Job is greater than 100ms then the Job is cancelled and preprocessor is called which will schedule the next job based on the current native slot instead of the corrupted endTransaction native slot.

When controller enters U/LPM mode with pending BC transaction, the zero length buffers for LE-ACL links are deallocated. In U/LPM resume flow, the pending BC transaction is scheduled before buffers are allocated, the scheduled BC transaction triggers FIQ immediately after getting scheduled and LC controller tries to access this zero length packet NULL buffer to transmit the packet.

The ZLP packet buffer are only deallocated in active to U/LPM state transition, in normal scenario it is not expected to be NULL or freed hence there was no NULL check, this causes system exception.

Fix: Fixed the ULPM wakeup sequence, schedule the pending BC transaction after LC resume is fully complete

column49:
This issue happened because of two issues in FW:
1. FW getting stuck for 32ms is root caused to be related to "pReq->dataLengthLimit" set to ZERO, which is part of SAM feature.
Whenever this is set to zero, FW, while programming the request, would set rx_start offset as ZERO, which is later used for programming DCMP to a past value (since offset is incorrect), causing FW getting stuck for ~32 ms (till DCNT counter wraps around).
2. When ATS is enabled, and FW sends out LMP AFH Request, then FW used to close ATS window right after getting baseband ACK for LMP_AFH_Req. This was because of ACU-u channel getting blocked when FW schedules to send LMP_AFT_Req even when we are only updating channel map, where as core spec mandates ACL-u to be blocked only when AFH is enabled or disabled, and not when channel map is changed.

Root caused ->  With transparent audio the buffer maintained is max of 90 bytes.  The interrupt rate at USB is requiring 24 to 26 bytes every 3 msec .  The  SP thread is supposed to provide the data from the ring buffer.

The issue happens when an USB ISR for SCO happens after SCO connection has been terminated. 

The exact issue is because of current logic where 0 bytes are read form Ring Buffer if SCO connections has been terminated and there are no active SCO connections. column4: [acer][Dorado][RS5] Intel 9560 vPRO wireless card BT throughput too low.
column49:
Root Cause:

Due to historic HW issue on BT (BT only catch the interrupt rising edge so need to toggle it after writing data to MBX in order BT will get interrupt to our MBX.),  there is WA for handling this issue that is done by using shrMbx infra :

o Read Status register of WIFI2BT. ---------->[ int1RegVal = (shrMbxHalIntrRead(MAILBOX_ID_WF2BT) ] 
o Clear Status register of WIFI2BT. ----------> [ shrMbxHalIntrClearBits(MAILBOX_ID_WF2BT, MBX_REG_DEFAULT_BITMASK) ] 
o Write to Cause register what we read & the new type we send now (DBGC MSG) --> [ shrMbxHalIntrWrite(MAILBOX_ID_WF2BT, (g_typesToSend | int1RegVal) << 8) ].

This write will set interrupt status bit and triggers interrupt rising edge for BT.

This above handling is done by using shrMbx Infra which is wrong due the READ & CLEAR function always approach BT2WIFI registers (offset from CNVI_AUX_MBX_MASTER_0_TO_1_STATUS) instead of WF2BT.

In bug WIFI-16623 this issue caused us to miss mbox rcv messages on power up flow since on power up flow we send DBGC message before handling the rcv messages and because of the bug we clear the interrupt bit of BT2WF instead of WF2BT.

In this scenario we got mbox message of TYPE2 and we try to send mbox message of type7. Before sending it we read the interrupt status register of BT2WF (instead of WF2BT) and we get bit2 set since we got mbox TYPE2 from BT. Then when we write to WF2BT status register we add the value we read (bit2) so BT gets interrupt of message TYPE2 although we didn't intend to send such message, and it reads data reg7 which contains garbage and ATS bit it set there.

[Dell][Pegatron][Vancouver][SKL][Win7] WHQL Lullaby Test (System)
column49:
Overall platform performance affects behavior of SCO disconnection and the passing rate of Lullaby2 test.


Disconnection process looks like this:
1. Issue SCO Disconnect
2. Wait for response from remote side
3. Disconnect audio device
4. Release SLC

Suspend/Resume handling was like this:
1. Get notification from system about transition to Sx state.
2. Get notification from system about Bluetooth is about to shutdown
3. Execute "Disconnection Process"
4. Get notification from system about wake up
5. Wait for audio device wake up
6. Initiate reconnection


The problem was on step 3 of "Suspend/Resume" handling: system entered sleep before step 2 of "Disconnection Process" was reached.

In turn, audio device was in "connected" state after wake up.
I.e., the following was happening:

1. System awakened
2. SCO Disconnection timed out
3. Audio device is disconnected
4. Reconnection procedure is started.
5. Audio device is in "connected" state again.

After wake up, Lullaby test was either reusing existing handle to audio device or was fast enough to open audio device before re-connection happened. In turn, Lullaby2 test was failing during/after re-connection happened (somewhere between steps 3 and 5).

In order to optimize the flow, the "Suspend/Resume" handling was changed in the following way:

Suspend/Resume handling was like this:
1. Get notification from system about transition to Sx state.
2. Execute "Disconnection Process"
3. Get notification from system about Bluetooth is about to shutdown
4. Get notification from system about wake up
5. Wait for audio device wake up
6. Initiate reconnection

I.e., we are initiating execution of "Disconnection Process" as soon as we got notificaton about transition to Sx state.

This helped to make sure that there will be no race after wake up.

LE connection job length is coded to be the entire connection interval. Issues fixed :
1. BT-55 fixes was enabled
2. Final Root Cause:
    Buffer release messages placed in BC event queue are getting overwritten. This could happen if the messages from BC are not processed in time by LC. So, in 0xA4, we are releasing the FHS buffers in IRQ context instead of waiting for LC to send a message to LLC to release the buffer. This will also be in accordance with the expectation in BC that these BB buffers are available always.

column4: [Huawei][Bell][Bluetooth] DUT stopped sending scan response after longer testing
column49:
since we are on ADV channel and share a common access code, it is possible for us to sync on a spurious ADV packet while we are actually expecting a Scan response.

We do have protection in our code to not accept that packet, but since we are saving the packet pointer, the Buffer allocated for the first ADV packet received would be overwritten. So, when we free the buffer in the post processor we will be freeing only the last allocated buffer which would be the spurious ADV.
If this happens one more time, we would lose one more buffer. Since we have 3 buffers for ADV/Scan activities, we would be down to 1 buffer, hence can service only the ADV and not the Scan response

[HP/SIO1386318][Damon 1.0/AVZ][KBL/8265/WIN10]WMP can't normally work and no sound send out from speaker after resume from S3 with BT speaker connect.
column49:
During D0Entry, iBTUSB driver sends HCI_Reset (added due to a known issue in WP2 B3/B4) before sending the HCI_Intel_Read_Version command to check if the device is running in bootloder or operational mode, depends on the previous device state and system state.
The logic in the iBTUSB to check this was broken for this scenario that the host shouldn't send HCI_Reset to the device when there was a active connection.
HCI_Reset resets the device and any connection but the host stack thinks the connection is still active.

This caused the error with "Unknown Connection Identifier" when the host stack sends the HCI command with that connection ID.
